blocks.text: The reactivity of Group 2 elements follows from their electronic configuration. They lose their two outer electrons (ns2) to form stable M2+ ions, which makes them react readily. Reactivity increases from beryllium to barium because the atoms grow larger, shielding increases and the ionization energy decreases, so the electrons are removed more easily.

blocks.alt: Five grey circles for the atoms Be, Mg, Ca, Sr and Ba drawn to scale from their metallic radii, 112, 160, 197, 215 and 222 pm, with the much smaller coloured M2+ ions below them, 31, 65, 99, 113 and 135 pm. An arrow says that left to right is down the group.
blocks.caption: Relative sizes of Group 2 atoms and ions (original diagram after Figure 17.1).
blocks.long_description: Down Group 2 each atom has one more shell of electrons, so the metallic radius grows from 112 pm for beryllium to 222 pm for barium. The outer ns2 electrons are further from the nucleus and better shielded, so the first and second ionization energies fall and the elements become more reactive. Each atom loses its two outer electrons to form an M2+ ion, which is much smaller than the atom because a whole shell is lost; the ions also grow down the group, from 31 pm for Be2+ to 135 pm for Ba2+.

blocks.title: Reactivity series of Group 2
blocks.text: Be < Mg < Ca < Sr < Ba: beryllium is the least reactive and barium the most reactive element of the group.

blocks.prompt: Arrange Mg, Ba and Ca in order of increasing reactivity.
blocks.explanation: Mg < Ca < Ba, following their positions down the group.

items: Group 2 metals lose two electrons to form M2+ ions.
Reactivity increases down the group: Be < Mg < Ca < Sr < Ba.
